subject: Coord: options to avoid late-night EU attendees for Acme demo
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Mike Thompson <mike.thompson@acme.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -0500
Subject: Demo availability next week — avoiding late EU hours

Hi Mike —

Thanks again for the interest and for sharing the high-level use case. We want to make sure the right engineering folks from our EU team can join without forcing them to be up at midnight. A few options below — happy to pick whatever works best for you and we can adjust presenters. All times include common conversions but let's use UTC to avoid DST confusion if needed.

Option A (single live session):
- Tue Mar 23, 2027 — 18:00 UTC (11:00 PT / 14:00 ET / 19:00 CET) — 45m
Option B (late US-friendly, EU-late):
- Wed Mar 24, 2027 — 00:00 UTC (17:00 PT / 20:00 ET / 21:00 CET) — 45m
Option C (split/overlap):
- Split into two connecting windows: 30m technical walkthrough at 16:00 UTC (09:00 PT / 12:00 ET / 17:00 CET) + 30m Q&A at 20:00 UTC (13:00 PT / 16:00 ET / 21:00 CET).

Attachments: acme-demo-agenda.pdf (draft), proposed_slots.ics (placeholder invites).

If you'd prefer a recorded run-through plus a short live Q&A timed for US working hours, we can do that too. Let me know which option you prefer and whether any of these specific times collide with your calendar.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
T: +1 415-555-0199

From: Mike Thompson <mike.thompson@acme.com>

Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo availability next week — avoiding late EU hours

Thanks Evelyn — appreciate the options. Our preferred slot is Tue Mar 23 at 12:00 PT (19:00 GMT-ish) because that lines up with our internal stakeholders on the West Coast. Unfortunately 21:00+ CET is rough for our counterparts in Amsterdam — they asked if there's any way to avoid asking them to join later than 19:30 CET.

Two quick asks: can we either (1) move the live demo earlier so EU can join before 20:00 CET, or (2) record the technical portion so EU can watch asynchronously and then join a short live Q&A at a Europe-friendly time? Option C sounds promising if the first window catches EU earlier.

-Mike
Mike Thompson
Dir. of Product — Acme Corp

Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 07:34:00 +0100

Hi Mike — thanks for the note. Quick technical suggestion from our side that might help: we can structure the session so the first 20 minutes are the product walkthrough (recorded or presented live) that covers the integration and performance characteristics you care about; the remaining 25 minutes are an open Q&A where EU engineers and our infra team can join in. That way EU only needs to join for the first (earlier) window, or they can watch the short recording and drop in for Q&A if needed.

Concretely I propose:
- Tue Mar 23: 16:00 UTC — 30m walkthrough (we record)
- Tue Mar 23: 18:00 UTC — 30m live Q&A with EU infra present (if they want)

If that split still pushes EU too late, we can flip the order (walkthrough earlier + Q&A earlier) and then do a second short overlap for US stakeholders. Happy to be flexible.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Mike —

Thanks — this is helpful. Hannah (my manager) asked me to propose a concrete plan that minimizes late EU hours while still letting your West Coast execs see the high-level flow. Suggestion:

- Tue Mar 23
  - 15:00 PT / 18:00 ET (22:00 CET) — 20m live executive overview (US-friendly time for execs but slightly late for EU)
  - 17:00 PT / 20:00 ET (02:00 CET next day) — NOT ideal — so instead we flip:

Better: split as Jonas suggested:
  - 16:00 UTC (09:00 PT / 12:00 ET / 17:00 CET) — 30m technical walkthrough (we record)
  - 18:00 UTC (11:00 PT / 14:00 ET / 19:00 CET) — 30m live Q&A (EU team can reasonably attend at 19:00 CET)

I'll send provisional calendar invites for those two windows and include the recording for any attendees who can't join live. If that works, please confirm and we'll lock it in.

Thanks,
Evelyn
